name: Bullpen — Part 4
description: What runs at the end of Part 4's build: the order lifecycle (accepted, working, partially filled, cancel requested, cancelled, filled, rejected) as a Postgres state machine in the trading schema, with a sweeper that finds stuck orders. Week one predicted a workflow engine; the build kept every step as one transaction in trading, and the sweeper is a daemon that calls a route, not a service with its own data. A signed-in player can place a market buy from the trading app and watch it move through its states; the sweeper is a Vercel Daemon, declared in vercel.json, that runs in production deployments.

nodes.name: Reader
nodes.description: A blog reader who lands on the public site to learn about Bullpen, and can now read its architecture page.

nodes.name: Player
nodes.description: A visitor who sees live crypto and end-of-day stock prices and the leaderboard. Signing in with GitHub gives a player an account; the order ticket, the orders list showing the seven states, and the lifecycle behind them are built and tested.

nodes.name: Bullpen Landing
nodes.description: The public landing site (apps/landing). Part 2 adds the /architecture page, which reads the repo's own records: the ADRs, the ADL, the CALM moments and the rules snapshot.

app-boundaries.description: An app never depends on another app, and imports a library only through its package entry point. Both are ADL rules that fail check:arch.

config.name: Components depend only on what they may
config.description: turbo boundaries enforces the IS DEPENDENT ON and HAS NO DEPENDENCY ON rules of structure.adl, direct and transitive, and reports a breach as the ASSERT it breaks.

config.name: Libraries are imported through their entry point
config.description: COMPONENTS use LIBRARIES ONLY THROUGH their package entry point: no @bullpen/ui/src/... and no relative path into packages/.

explorer-matches-model.description: What the architecture explorer draws has to be this model. Part 2's explorer content is checked against this file, not against the prediction.

config.name: The explorer matches the model
config.description: Every explorer node and edge exists in its CALM document, and every CALM node is drawn.

nodes.name: Bullpen Trading App
nodes.description: The trading app: it owns orders and their lifecycle, reservations, fills, the ledger, positions and the leaderboard view in the trading schema, shows end-of-day stock prices read through prices_v1, signs players in with GitHub, and serves the authenticated sweep route the sweeper calls.

price-contract-only.description: trading READS market_data ONLY THROUGH market_data.prices_v1: no grant on any market_data table.

config.name: Prices only through the contract
config.description: trading READS market_data ONLY THROUGH market_data.prices_v1: no grant on any market_data table.

nodes.name: CoinGecko
nodes.description: CoinGecko's free Demo API (api.coingecko.com), called for BTC-USD price snapshots. Chosen after a Coinbase-based design was ruled out by Coinbase's Terms of Use, which forbid public display of their data (see issue #6, ADR-0005, docs/data-sources.md).

nodes.name: Google Analytics 4
nodes.description: Google's product analytics (gtag.js from www.googletagmanager.com), loaded in the visitor's browser by both apps only after they accept and only in production. Receives page views and four custom events with no personal data. Consent Mode starts denied for all four signals; only analytics_storage is ever granted, and the advertising signals never are (see ADR-0010).

analytics-consent.description: Nothing loads and no cookie is set until the visitor accepts; advertising signals are always denied.

config.name: Analytics only after consent
config.description: packages/ui's Analytics loads the Google tag only after Accept, with the Consent Mode default (all four denied) queued first and ad_storage, ad_user_data and ad_personalization never granted.

nodes.name: Microsoft Clarity
nodes.description: Microsoft's heatmaps and session recordings (www.clarity.ms), loaded in the visitor's browser by both apps only after they accept and only in production. Receives the Consent API v2 signal with advertising storage denied, and a part tag. Form fields are masked (see ADR-0010).

analytics-consent.description: Nothing loads and no cookie is set until the visitor accepts; advertising storage is always denied.

config.name: Analytics only after consent
config.description: packages/ui's Analytics loads the Clarity tag only after Accept, with Consent API v2 queued first: ad_Storage denied, analytics_Storage granted.

nodes.name: Market Data Service
nodes.description: The single owner of market data: both providers (stocks end of day, crypto) and both call budgets. It serves the public price route and the daily ingest. It is a boundary inside one release, not an independently deployed microservice.

secret-containment.description: The provider keys, the cron secret and the database URL stay in one place: only this service reads them. Everything else in apps/ and packages/ fails check:arch if it names them in code.

config.name: The market-data secrets are read in one place
config.description: ONLY apps/market-data/src READS COINGECKO_DEMO_API_KEY. ONLY apps/market-data/src READS ALPHA_VANTAGE_API_KEY. ONLY apps/market-data/src READS CRON_SECRET.

call-budget.description: A call ledger caps stock calls at 20 a provider-day and crypto at 9,000 a month; a call over the cap is refused before it leaves the process. CoinGecko's monthly volume is also modelled against its allowance.

config.name: Every provider call is counted before it leaves
config.description: A call ledger caps stock calls at 20 a provider-day and crypto at 9,000 a month; a call over the cap is refused before it leaves the process. CoinGecko's monthly volume is also modelled against its allowance.

nodes.name: Bullpen Database
nodes.description: One Neon Postgres project and one database. A schema and a plain database role per transactional owner: market_data (market_data_owner) and trading (trading_owner), with one read-only view, market_data.prices_v1, between them. Orders and the ledger stay in one transaction.

owner-roles.description: ONLY market-data WRITES market_data. ONLY trading WRITES trading.orders AND trading.ledger. The runtime roles are plain: no superuser, no bypass, no membership of a role that reads every schema.

config.name: One writer per schema
config.description: ONLY market-data WRITES market_data. ONLY trading WRITES trading.orders AND trading.ledger. The runtime roles are plain: no superuser, no bypass, no membership of a role that reads every schema.

migration-folders.description: A migration in one owner's folder that names the other owner's schema fails the build, and fails in the database because each folder runs as its own owner.

config.name: A migration touches only its own schema
config.description: A migration in one owner's folder that names the other owner's schema fails the build, and fails in the database because each folder runs as its own owner.

nodes.name: Alpha Vantage
nodes.description: External market-data API for U.S. stock prices: end of day, one request per symbol, fetched once a day by the Market Data service within a daily call budget (ADR-0008).

status-aware-drift-check.description: A node that names a provider is held to an Accepted ADR: a Proposed one counts as undecided and fails the build (ADR-0016).

config.name: The drift check is status-aware
config.description: A node that names a provider is held to an Accepted ADR: a Proposed one counts as undecided and fails the build (ADR-0016).

nodes.name: Daily ingest cron
nodes.description: Vercel's scheduler: once a day after the U.S. close it calls the Market Data service's ingest, with a secret.

nodes.name: market_data schema
nodes.description: Schema market_data, owned by the role market_data_owner: quotes, the provider call ledger, and the view prices_v1.

nodes.name: trading schema
nodes.description: Accounts, orders with a state and a version, reservations, fills, order events, the ledger, positions and the leaderboard view. Every step of an order's life is one transaction here.

reconciliation-check.description: The materialized view must equal the same ranking computed on read from the source tables; the check names the account and both values when they differ. It runs in CI's database tests.

config.name: The leaderboard view equals its source
config.description: The materialized view must equal the same ranking computed on read from the source tables; the check names the account and both values when they differ. It runs in CI's database tests.

nodes.name: market_data.prices_v1
nodes.description: The price contract: symbol, price, as-of time, source and a stale flag, read-only. The only thing outside market_data that trading may read.

nodes.name: Sweeper
nodes.description: A Vercel Daemon whose only job is to call the Trading App's sweep route and wait: every 5 seconds while an order is open, backing off to every 60 minutes when none is. It reads no database URL and holds no data. It is built and tested locally, declared in vercel.json, and runs in production deployments only.

secret-containment.description: The sweeper's token stays in one place: only this daemon's source reads it. The route's secret is read only by the trading app's own directory.

config.name: The sweep secrets are read in one place each
config.description: ONLY apps/sweeper/src READS SWEEPER_TOKEN. ONLY apps/web/app/lib/trading READS SWEEP_SECRET.

nodes.name: Neon Auth
nodes.description: Neon's managed sign-in, enabled on the production branch with GitHub as its only provider. The trading app checks the access token it issues against its public keys and stores only the user's id.
